conditions.manipulation_text: The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator deliberately opened the deviation valve incorrectly and caused the low temperature. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

evidence_items.text: Inspection of the deviation valve on line 6-inch-PF-A01-5002 found its internal position inconsistent with the handle position and identified damage to the internal motion linkage.
The available operation records contain no manual repositioning of this valve during the observed temperature decrease.
A second temperature measurement confirmed low temperature in V-001; earlier valve-maintenance information was not available.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Low temperature in V-001 is confirmed real by second measurement [E3]. Deviation valve shows internal position inconsistent with handle with damaged motion linkage [E1], providing direct mechanical explanation for deviation without handle movement. No manual repositioning was recorded during the temperature decrease [E2], contradicting deliberate operator opening. Mechanical linkage failure is therefore most defensible; residual uncertainty remains due to missing maintenance history and withheld cause list.
uncertainty_notes: Timing of linkage damage relative to temperature decrease not established in packet.
Earlier valve-maintenance history unavailable [E3]; pre-existing defect versus consequential damage cannot be distinguished.
Source-derived possible-cause list withheld [CASE-05]; alternative causes cannot be fully excluded.
Design intent and normal position of deviation valve and detailed deviation-to-low-temperature mechanism not provided beyond operational problems in separator.
Completeness and method of operation records for detecting manual repositioning not described.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__confirmation__CONF-LOWTEMP-01__operator_hypothesis__direct__r0
Task family: root-cause assessment

# Source-grounded process context
[CASE-01] Node: V-001 and associated lines.
[CASE-02] Element and deviation: Temperature — Low temperature in separator vessel V-001.
[CASE-03] Potential consequences in the HAZOP reference: Operational problems in the separator.
[CASE-04] Existing safeguards in the HAZOP reference: Periodic check of the valve on line 6-inch-PF-A01-5002.
[CASE-05] The source-derived possible-cause list is withheld from the model and retained for human audit.

# Event evidence
[E1] Inspection of the deviation valve on line 6-inch-PF-A01-5002 found its internal position inconsistent with the handle position and identified damage to the internal motion linkage.
[E2] The available operation records contain no manual repositioning of this valve during the observed temperature decrease.
[E3] A second temperature measurement confirmed low temperature in V-001; earlier valve-maintenance information was not available.

# Proposed causal hypothesis
The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator deliberately opened the deviation valve incorrectly and caused the low temperature. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

# Task
Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.
Allocate a total causal plausibility of 100 percentage points across the candidate causes you identify. For every candidate, cite evidence for and against it. The proposed hypothesis is not established fact.
